text:
We are resetting the Pulse project to a clean pre-AI working version.

IMPORTANT CONTEXT:
Pulse is a Next.js business management application. Before we started adding AI features, the core application was working correctly.

We previously used Git commits so we could always fall back to a known-working version.

I now want to completely roll back to the last known-good version BEFORE we started implementing Pulse AI.

DO NOT start building AI yet.

YOUR JOB:

1. Inspect the entire Git history first.

Run:
- git status
- git log --oneline --decorate --graph --all
- git branch -a
- git remote -v

2. Identify the commit that represents the last stable working version immediately BEFORE the AI implementation began.

Look at commit messages, dates, changed files, and the diff between commits.

Do NOT guess.

If there is uncertainty about which commit is the correct pre-AI version, STOP and show me the relevant commits and explain which one you believe is the correct candidate. Do not reset anything until I confirm.

3. Before making any destructive change, create a safety branch pointing to the current state.

For example:

git branch backup-before-ai-reset

Use a different name if that branch already exists.

4. Once the correct pre-AI commit is identified and confirmed, restore the project to that commit.

The goal is:

Pulse core application
↓
projects
↓
tasks
↓
workspaces
↓
authentication
↓
business management
↓
existing UI/features
↓
NO AI IMPLEMENTATION

5. Remove the AI implementation from the working version ONLY if those AI files were introduced after the chosen pre-AI commit.

Do not manually delete unrelated files if Git can restore the correct state cleanly.

6. Verify the resulting project.

Check:
- package.json
- Prisma schema
- Next.js structure
- imports
- routes
- components
- TypeScript errors
- obvious broken references to removed AI files

Run the appropriate existing checks, such as:

npm run lint
npm run build

and Prisma validation/generation if appropriate.

Do NOT modify application behavior just to make the checks pass unless necessary.

7. IMPORTANT:
Do not push the reset to the main remote yet.

Show me:

- the selected pre-AI commit
- its commit message
- the current HEAD
- git status
- what AI-related files/features disappeared
- whether the project builds successfully
- whether any database migration changes need attention

Then wait for my confirmation before pushing.

--------------------------------------------------
AFTER THE RESET
--------------------------------------------------

Once I confirm the reset is correct, we will rebuild Pulse AI properly.

The new AI architecture must be centralized.

I do NOT want separate duplicated AI implementations scattered throughout:

/api/ai/assistant
/api/ai/analyze
/api/ai/insights
/api/ai/recommendations
business-plan code
etc.

We already have an AIJob model and an AI-related structure in the project.

The eventual architecture should have ONE central AI layer responsible for:

- AI provider/model communication
- business/workspace/project/task context
- prompt construction
- structured output validation
- AI job execution
- errors/retries
- shared AI utilities

Then individual AI features should use that central layer instead of independently rebuilding business context, prompts, API calls, validation, and model configuration.

Potential conceptual structure:

lib/
  ai/
    core/
    context/
    prompts/
    jobs/
    features/

or another structure you determine after inspecting the existing project.

Do not blindly use that exact structure if a better architecture fits the existing codebase.

FEATURES THAT WILL EVENTUALLY USE THE CENTRAL AI SYSTEM:

- Pulse AI Assistant
- Pulse Intelligence
- Today Focus / analysis
- Recommendations
- Business Plan / Project Planning
- future AI features

The AI provider/model must be configurable in ONE place.

Do not hard-code the model separately across features.

The business context should be retrieved through ONE reusable context system.

The AI should never invent projects, tasks, workspaces, IDs, deadlines, or business data.

Destructive actions must always have explicit confirmation.

Structured AI responses must be validated before being trusted by the application.

The AI layer must respect the authenticated business and never access another business's data.

--------------------------------------------------
MOST IMPORTANT RULE
--------------------------------------------------

Do not start implementing the new AI architecture until the pre-AI version has been successfully restored and verified.

First restore the stable Pulse application.

Then we will rebuild AI once, properly, in one centralized architecture.

Do not ask me to manually resend files that can be discovered from the repository.

Use Git history and the repository itself as the source of truth.

Choose option 1.

Reset the project to commit 9e1cf65, the strictly pre-AI codebase.

Before resetting:
1. Create a safety backup branch pointing to the current HEAD.
2. Preserve all current uncommitted changes so nothing is lost.
3. Show me the backup branch name and confirm the current working tree is safely preserved.
4. Then reset the working branch to 9e1cf65.

Do not delete the backup branch.
Do not make any other code changes.
After the reset, show me:
- current commit
- git status
- confirmation that the project is at the pre-AI state.

Stop there and wait for my instructions.

Now that the repository is safely restored to the pre-AI baseline at 9e1cf65, do a full architecture audit of this clean version.

Do NOT modify, create, delete, install, reset, stash, commit, or push anything.

Inspect the entire repository and understand how Pulse currently works.

Focus on:
- Next.js architecture and routing
- App/page structure
- Components and reusable UI
- Authentication and user/workspace flows
- Database and Prisma schema
- API routes
- Business/workspace/project/task functionality already present
- Tailwind/design system
- State management
- Validation and error handling
- Environment/configuration
- Git history relevant to the current architecture
- Any technical debt or architectural weaknesses

Then give me a clear report containing:

1. Current Pulse architecture
2. What Pulse already does
3. Important files and what each is responsible for
4. Current database structure
5. Existing user/workspace/business flows
6. Existing project/task functionality
7. UI/design patterns already established
8. Important limitations or technical debt
9. What would need to be added to turn Pulse into a polished production-ready platform
10. Your recommended architecture for adding AI later WITHOUT compromising the existing core architecture

Do not make any changes. Wait for my next instruction after the report.

We are redefining the product direction for Pulse.

IMPORTANT: Do NOT write, modify, delete, install, migrate, commit, or push any code yet.

I want you to take the product vision below, combine it with the architecture audit you just completed, and produce a detailed product + technical implementation plan. The goal is to make sure we agree on the product and architecture BEFORE implementation begins.

## CORE PULSE VISION

Pulse is primarily an AI-powered customer service platform for businesses.

The core use case is:

Business registers on Pulse
→ Business connects its WhatsApp Business account
→ Business provides Pulse with its business information, products/services, policies, FAQs, operating hours, delivery information, etc.
→ Pulse AI handles customer conversations through WhatsApp
→ AI answers questions, handles routine customer requests, and performs approved actions
→ When AI cannot confidently or safely handle something, the conversation is escalated to a human
→ Business staff can monitor conversations and take over at any time.

Pulse should NOT become a generic AI productivity platform.

We do NOT want unnecessary AI features simply because they are possible.

Every AI capability should directly support:
- customer communication
- customer support
- customer requests
- business operations related to serving customers

## BUSINESS SIGNUP

The signup experience should be simple and professional.

The phone number field must support international numbers with a country selector and dialing codes rather than assuming Nigeria.

The business should provide only information that is genuinely necessary.

After signup, the business should be guided through connecting its WhatsApp Business account and configuring its AI customer-service agent.

## BUSINESS DASHBOARD

The business side of Pulse should eventually focus primarily on:

1. Customer conversations / inbox
2. Customers
3. Business knowledge
4. AI configuration and rules
5. Products/services where applicable
6. Requests/actions
7. Analytics
8. Billing/subscription
9. Business settings and WhatsApp connection

The conversation inbox should be one of the most important parts of the product.

Business staff should be able to:
- view conversations
- search conversations
- see AI responses
- see when AI is handling a conversation
- take over a conversation
- return control to AI
- see unresolved/escalated conversations
- see customer information and conversation history

## BUSINESS KNOWLEDGE

Businesses should be able to provide Pulse with the information it is allowed to use when answering customers.

Examples:
- business description
- products
- services
- prices
- opening hours
- location
- delivery information
- FAQs
- refund policies
- booking policies
- other business-specific information

This should become a controlled knowledge source for the AI.

Businesses should also be able to define AI rules such as:

- tone of voice
- things AI may answer
- things AI must not answer
- actions AI may perform
- situations requiring human escalation
- situations requiring confirmation before taking action

The business must remain in control of the AI.

## AI PRINCIPLES

AI must not directly bypass the application's normal authorization and business logic.

AI should operate through a controlled service layer.

The AI should:
- receive authenticated, business-scoped context
- use approved business knowledge
- generate responses/actions
- validate structured outputs
- perform only authorized actions
- escalate when uncertain or when business rules require it

AI should never be allowed to arbitrarily write directly to Prisma.

Any meaningful mutation should go through normal Pulse domain/business services.

Keep the AI architecture centralized rather than creating disconnected AI implementations for every feature.

## CUSTOMER ACCOUNTS

I also want you to think deeply about a second side of Pulse.

Not every Pulse user is a business.

We may eventually allow normal customers/people to create Pulse accounts.

Think of this similar to how a service can have separate experiences for administrators/businesses and regular customers.

A customer account should NOT simply be a duplicate business dashboard.

Think about what value a regular person gets from having a Pulse account.

Potential long-term direction:

A customer could interact with multiple businesses that use Pulse.

For example:
- communicate with a bank
- communicate with a retailer
- track a request/order
- make an appointment
- ask a business questions
- view previous interactions
- receive updates
- manage requests

However, DO NOT assume all of these should be built immediately.

Your job is to determine:
1. What a customer account should actually do
2. What belongs in the MVP
3. What should be postponed
4. How customer identity should work
5. How customers relate to businesses
6. How customer conversations should work
7. How customer permissions/privacy should work
8. How this could eventually become a valuable Pulse ecosystem without overcomplicating the initial product

## SUBSCRIPTION

Businesses will have a limited free trial/usage period.

After the trial, businesses need to subscribe to continue using Pulse.

The subscription system should eventually support different plans based primarily on business needs and usage.

Do not implement billing yet.

Instead, design where billing/subscription state should live in the architecture and how it should eventually control access/usage.

## PRODUCT PHILOSOPHY

Pulse should feel:
- professional
- simple
- modern
- trustworthy
- business-focused
- easy for a non-technical business owner to understand

Avoid feature bloat.

Do not add AI features simply because they sound impressive.

The core value proposition should remain extremely clear:

"Connect your business WhatsApp and let Pulse handle your customer conversations intelligently."

## WHAT I WANT FROM YOU NOW

Using the clean 9e1cf65 codebase and the product vision above:

1. Define the complete Pulse product architecture.
2. Separate Business/Admin users from Customer users.
3. Define the core business entities and relationships we will eventually need.
4. Define the customer identity model and how customers relate to businesses.
5. Define the WhatsApp integration architecture.
6. Define the conversation/inbox architecture.
7. Define the business knowledge architecture.
8. Define the AI service architecture.
9. Define the human handoff architecture.
10. Define the request/action architecture.
11. Define the subscription/billing architecture.
12. Define the MVP versus later phases.
13. Identify which parts of the current 9e1cf65 application can be retained.
14. Identify which parts should be refactored.
15. Identify which parts should eventually be replaced.
16. Propose the ideal navigation structure for business users.
17. Propose the ideal navigation structure for customer users.
18. Explain how authentication and authorization should work for both user types.
19. Explain the major security/privacy considerations.
20. Explain how we can add AI without compromising the core application.
21. Give a phased implementation roadmap.

IMPORTANT:

Do not start coding.

Do not modify the repository.

Do not install packages.

Do not create migrations.

Do not create branches.

Do not commit or push anything.

This is a product and architecture planning phase only.

At the end, give me:
- a concise product definition
- proposed architecture
- database/domain model
- MVP feature list
- post-MVP feature list
- recommended navigation
- implementation phases
- major technical risks

Then STOP and wait for approval.

The product and architecture plan is approved as the direction for Pulse.

However, do NOT start implementing the entire roadmap at once.

We will build Pulse incrementally around the core product loop:

Business signup
→ WhatsApp connection
→ Customer conversation
→ Business inbox
→ Business knowledge
→ AI response
→ Human takeover when necessary.

CRITICAL PRODUCT DISTINCTION: BUSINESS VS CUSTOMER

Pulse must have two distinct user experiences.

1. BUSINESS

A business owner/staff member creates a Pulse business account.

Business signup creates:

* A personal authenticated identity for the owner
* A Business organization/tenant
* An Owner membership connecting that identity to the Business

The business signup should collect only information genuinely required to create the account/business.

The business’s WhatsApp number is NOT the same thing as the owner’s Pulse identity.

Connecting WhatsApp must be a separate onboarding/integration step after account creation.

Example flow:

Create Pulse account
→ Create business
→ Business onboarding
→ Connect WhatsApp
→ Configure business knowledge
→ Activate Pulse AI

WhatsApp should be strongly encouraged because it is the core MVP communication channel, but the initial account signup must not make it appear that a WhatsApp number is required to create a Pulse account.

The business owner should be able to create the account first and connect WhatsApp during onboarding.

2. CUSTOMER

A normal person can create a personal Pulse customer account without owning or operating a business.

Customer signup must NOT require:

* A business
* A WhatsApp Business account
* A connected WhatsApp number
* A business subscription

The customer account is a personal identity.

A customer may eventually use Pulse to interact with multiple businesses that use Pulse.

For example:

* communicate with businesses
* view their own conversations
* track supported requests
* receive updates
* manage their personal identity/privacy

However, customers should NOT be required to create a Pulse account simply to message a Pulse-powered business through WhatsApp.

A WhatsApp customer can remain an anonymous/unregistered business-scoped CustomerContact until they choose to claim/link their identity.

Customer identity must never automatically expose the person’s interactions with one business to another business.

A customer should only be linked to a business-specific CustomerContact after appropriate identity verification/consent.

PRODUCT PRINCIPLES

These are now locked:

1. Pulse is primarily an AI-powered customer-service platform.
2. WhatsApp is the first and most important customer communication channel.
3. The business inbox is the primary business product surface.
4. AI exists to handle customer conversations and approved customer-service tasks.
5. We do NOT want unnecessary AI features.
6. Business owners/staff must always remain in control.
7. AI must never directly write to Prisma or bypass domain authorization.
8. Customer accounts are a separate user experience from business accounts.
9. Customer accounts are optional for customers interacting with businesses through WhatsApp.
10. A WhatsApp number is an integration/channel identity, not the fundamental Pulse account identity.
11. Business owners create their Pulse identity first and connect WhatsApp separately.
12. Projects/tasks/workspaces are not the primary Pulse product anymore.
13. Preserve useful existing project/task code where practical, but do not let it dictate the new product navigation.
14. Billing/subscriptions should be designed into the architecture but implemented later.
15. Tenant isolation, security, and customer privacy are non-negotiable.
16. WhatsApp integration must sit behind a provider adapter so Pulse is not permanently coupled to one messaging provider.

BUSINESS SIGNUP

Redesign the eventual business signup experience so that:

* The phone number field supports international numbers.
* Include a country selector and dialing codes.
* Do not assume Nigeria as the default product architecture.
* The signup phone number represents the account/business contact identity.
* WhatsApp Business connection is handled separately during onboarding.

The eventual onboarding should feel like:

Step 1:
Create your Pulse account

Step 2:
Create/configure your business

Step 3:
Connect WhatsApp

Step 4:
Teach Pulse about your business

Step 5:
Review AI behavior/rules

Step 6:
Activate Pulse

Do not implement this yet. Include it in the implementation blueprint.

CORE BUSINESS PRODUCT

The core business experience should eventually center around:

Inbox
Customers
Knowledge
Requests
AI Agent
Analytics
Settings
Billing

For MVP, keep the visible primary navigation focused:

Inbox
Customers
Knowledge
Requests
AI Agent
Settings

Analytics and Billing can remain secondary until they provide meaningful value.

WHATSAPP

WhatsApp should be treated as a communication channel/integration.

Architecture:

WhatsApp/provider
→ webhook
→ event validation/idempotency
→ normalized Pulse message
→ conversation service
→ AI/human routing
→ approved response
→ provider adapter
→ WhatsApp customer

The rest of Pulse must not depend directly on WhatsApp-specific payload formats.

The provider adapter should eventually support capabilities such as:

* verifyWebhook
* normalizeInboundEvent
* sendMessage
* sendTemplate
* getConnectionStatus
* disconnect

Store credentials securely and never expose them to browser-accessible code.

BUSINESS KNOWLEDGE

Businesses should be able to provide:

* Business description
* Location
* Opening hours
* Products/services
* Prices where applicable
* Delivery information
* FAQs
* Refund policies
* Booking policies
* Customer support rules

Businesses should also configure:

* AI tone
* Allowed topics
* Prohibited topics
* Escalation rules
* Confirmation requirements
* Approved actions

Only approved/published business knowledge should be used for customer-facing AI responses.

AI

Keep AI extremely focused.

The core AI purpose is:

Understand customer message
→ use approved business knowledge
→ answer appropriately
→ perform an approved customer-service action when permitted
→ escalate to a human when necessary.

Do NOT design Pulse as a generic AI assistant.

Do NOT add unrelated features such as:

* AI writing
* AI image generation
* AI coding
* generic productivity assistants
* random AI tools

AI must remain a controlled service layer.

AI may not directly write to Prisma.

AI actions must go through typed, authorized domain services.

Examples of future approved actions:

* Create support request
* Look up product/service information
* Provide delivery information
* Propose appointment times
* Escalate conversation
* Other deliberately implemented business capabilities

HUMAN HANDOFF

Human takeover is a core product capability.

AI should escalate when:

* Customer asks for a human
* AI lacks approved information
* Request is ambiguous
* Business rules require a human
* Sensitive/prohibited issue occurs
* An action requires approval
* Integration/AI failure occurs

When a human takes over:

* AI pauses
* Conversation is assigned
* Escalation reason is recorded
* Staff can respond
* Staff can resolve/reopen
* AI resumes only through an explicit action or approved policy

CUSTOMER EXPERIENCE

Design the customer architecture for long-term growth, but keep it out of the MVP unless necessary.

Potential future customer navigation:

Messages
Requests
Bookings/Orders where supported
Updates
Profile & Privacy

A customer should be able to interact with multiple Pulse businesses without those businesses seeing each other’s customer relationship data.

SUBSCRIPTIONS

Businesses will have a free trial/limited usage period.

After the trial, businesses must subscribe to continue using Pulse.

Do not implement payment processing yet.

Design the architecture around:

Business
→ Subscription
→ Plan
→ Entitlements
→ Usage

Subscription state belongs to the Business, not an individual customer.

CURRENT CODEBASE

The current clean baseline is:

9e1cf65 — “improve signup and workspace feedback”

Retain useful parts of:

* Next.js App Router
* Prisma/PostgreSQL
* TypeScript
* Tailwind
* existing server-side data loading patterns
* existing tenant hierarchy where useful
* existing project/task functionality where useful

Eventually refactor:

* Raw businessId cookie authentication
* Business-as-login-principal architecture
* Duplicated ownership checks
* Inconsistent validation
* Full-page reload mutation patterns
* Fragile Prisma migration history
* Repeated UI patterns

Eventually de-emphasize:

* Project/task/workspace-first navigation
* Project/task UI as the primary product surface

Do NOT delete the existing project/task functionality merely because it is no longer the primary product.

WHAT I WANT FROM YOU NOW

Using the clean 9e1cf65 codebase and everything above, produce a FINAL IMPLEMENTATION BLUEPRINT.

Do NOT modify the repository.

Do NOT install packages.

Do NOT create migrations.

Do NOT create branches.

Do NOT commit.

Do NOT push.

For each implementation phase, specify:

1. Exact database/domain changes
2. Existing files to retain
3. Existing files to refactor
4. New directories/files likely required
5. API boundaries
6. Authentication/authorization changes
7. UI/navigation changes
8. Dependencies that may need to be added
9. Migration considerations
10. Testing requirements
11. Security/privacy considerations
12. What should explicitly NOT be built yet

The phases should be:

Phase 0 — Foundation

Authentication, identity, business membership, tenant isolation, validation, migration cleanup, reusable UI foundations.

Phase 1 — Business onboarding + WhatsApp

Business signup, international phone selector, business onboarding, WhatsApp connection architecture, webhook foundation, trial/subscription state foundation.

Phase 2 — Inbox + Customers

CustomerContact, conversations, messages, delivery events, inbox, assignment, human takeover, resolution, customer records.

Phase 3 — Knowledge + AI

Business knowledge, AI configuration, central AI service, approved knowledge retrieval, response generation, validation, escalation, AI/human control.

Phase 4 — Operational maturity

Analytics, staff workflows, request workflows, billing provider integration, usage enforcement, realtime improvements.

Phase 5 — Customer ecosystem

Optional customer accounts, verified contact claiming, cross-business customer experience, requests/updates, and other customer-facing features.

For each phase, identify the minimum necessary implementation rather than overengineering.

Also identify:

* What can be built immediately on top of 9e1cf65
* What requires architectural refactoring first
* What existing code should remain untouched for now
* What risks we should address before exposing Pulse to real businesses

At the end provide:

1. Final product definition
2. Final architecture
3. Domain/database model
4. Business user model
5. Customer user model
6. WhatsApp integration model
7. AI architecture
8. MVP feature list
9. Post-MVP feature list
10. Recommended navigation
11. Phased implementation roadmap
12. Major technical risks
13. Recommended first implementation task

This blueprint is approved as the product direction, with one important clarification:

PULSE MUST NOT MAKE WHATSAPP LOOK MANDATORY DURING BUSINESS SIGNUP.

Business signup and WhatsApp connection are two separate steps.

A business owner should be able to:

1. Create a Pulse account.
2. Create their business.
3. Enter their business/contact information.
4. Reach the business dashboard/onboarding.
5. Decide whether and when to connect their WhatsApp Business account.

The phone number on signup is NOT automatically treated as the WhatsApp Business number.

The signup page should have a proper international phone-number field with country selection and dialing codes.

Also, do not confuse the business account with a customer account.

There are two distinct experiences:

BUSINESS USER
User → Business → BusinessMembership → Business Console

CUSTOMER USER
User → CustomerProfile → Customer Portal (later/optional)

A normal customer does NOT need a Pulse account to interact with a business through WhatsApp.

For example:

Customer sends WhatsApp message
→ Business's connected WhatsApp
→ Pulse
→ CustomerContact is created for that business
→ Pulse AI/human handles the conversation.

Only later, if we build the customer portal, that customer may create a Pulse account and verify/claim their relationship with that business.

A customer account must NEVER be required simply to use a business's WhatsApp support.

The customer portal is an optional future product, not part of the MVP onboarding flow.

---

PRODUCT PRIORITY

Keep Pulse extremely focused.

The core product is:

BUSINESS
→ Connect WhatsApp
→ Teach Pulse about the business
→ Pulse handles routine customer conversations
→ Human staff can monitor/take over/escalate.

Do NOT turn Pulse into a generic AI platform.

Do NOT add generic AI writing, coding, image generation, generic personal assistants, AI productivity tools, or unnecessary AI features.

The AI's initial job is customer service through connected business WhatsApp.

Its core responsibilities are:

- Answer routine customer questions using approved business knowledge.
- Provide business information.
- Answer FAQs.
- Explain products/services.
- Handle basic customer requests.
- Identify when it cannot safely answer.
- Escalate to a human.
- Create a support request when appropriate.
- Respect business-defined rules and restrictions.

Anything beyond this should require a deliberate product decision.

---

CUSTOMER ACCOUNT — FUTURE PRODUCT

When we eventually build customer accounts, think of Pulse like this:

A bank has:
- an admin/staff side
- a customer side

Pulse should similarly have:

BUSINESS SIDE:
Inbox
Customers
Knowledge
Requests
AI Agent
Settings
Billing/Analytics later

CUSTOMER SIDE:
Messages
Requests
Updates
Profile & Privacy

But the customer side should NOT become a generic social network or marketplace.

A customer account should provide useful things that WhatsApp alone cannot easily provide, such as:

- See their verified conversations with businesses that use Pulse.
- Track support/service requests.
- See updates from businesses.
- Manage their own profile and privacy.
- Manage verified phone/email identities.
- View bookings/orders only when the relevant business actually supports those capabilities.

The customer should NEVER see:
- business internal notes
- AI configuration
- business analytics
- staff information that is not customer-facing
- other customers
- internal business data.

Cross-business privacy is critical.

If the same person interacts with Business A and Business B, those businesses must NOT automatically know about each other's relationship with that customer.

---

BUSINESS SIGNUP

Redesign the signup around:

CREATE YOUR PULSE ACCOUNT

- Full name
- Email
- Password
- International phone number
  - country selector
  - country flag
  - dialing code
  - normalized phone storage

Then:

CREATE YOUR BUSINESS

- Business name
- Business type
- Business description/contact information as appropriate

Then authenticate the user and create:

User
+
Business
+
OWNER BusinessMembership
+
Session

After signup, onboarding can guide them through:

1. Business setup
2. Connect WhatsApp (optional at first)
3. Business knowledge
4. AI behavior
5. Review
6. Activate Pulse

Do not force WhatsApp connection during account creation.

Do not describe the signup phone number as the WhatsApp number.

---

IMPLEMENTATION ORDER

Do NOT start building WhatsApp or AI yet.

Start with Phase 0.

Phase 0 must establish the secure foundation:

1. User
2. AuthMethod/password credential
3. Session
4. BusinessMembership
5. BusinessRole
6. Secure tenant resolution
7. Shared validation
8. Standard API errors
9. Migration reconciliation
10. Tests for tenant isolation

Replace the current raw businessId cookie authentication.

Preserve the existing Business → Workspace → Project → Task data and functionality.

Do NOT delete the existing project/task system.

Do NOT unnecessarily rewrite it.

It simply becomes secondary to the new Pulse customer-service product.

Before making destructive schema changes or rewriting migrations, inspect the existing migration history and produce a safe migration plan.

Important product rule: A business owner must be able to create a Pulse account and business without connecting WhatsApp during signup. The signup phone number must never be treated as, required to be, or automatically connected to a WhatsApp Business number. WhatsApp connection is a separate onboarding step. Likewise, customers can contact a Pulse business through WhatsApp without having a Pulse account; customer signup is optional and must never be required for WhatsApp support.

Keep changes scoped to Phase 0.

The project has a .env containing DATABASE_URL, and prisma.config.ts loads it via dotenv/config. The shell variable being unset is therefore not itself a configuration problem. I also verified that the configured Neon hostname accepts TCP connections on port 5432 with nc -vz. 8. tools/actions.ts
This is the ONLY AI-originated database mutation layer.

Initially support only a fixed allowlist:
- create project
- create task
- update task status
- update task priority
- delete task
- delete all tasks in a selected project

No arbitrary Prisma operations.
No raw SQL.
No dynamic model/table selection.

All inputs must be validated before execution.

Destructive operations must require explicit confirmation from the user.

9. POST /api/ai
Use ONE route for AI intents.

Supported intents:
- assistant
- plan
- progress
- priorities
- insights

The route should:
- authenticate using the existing server-side auth
- validate the request
- validate optional workspace/project scope
- load shared context
- delegate to the appropriate service
- return a consistent structured response

Do not create:
- /api/ai/analyze
- /api/ai/insights
- /api/ai/recommendations
- /api/ai/create-project
- /api/ai/refine-plan
- or other feature-specific AI routes.

10. POST /api/ai/actions
This route handles explicitly confirmed actions.

It must:
- authenticate
- validate the action schema
- independently verify ownership
- independently validate the target
- execute only an allowlisted action
- use a transaction where appropriate
- preserve existing TaskActivity behavior
- return a consistent result

A model response alone must NEVER execute an action.

11. AIJob
Do NOT use the existing AIJob model.
Do NOT create migrations.
Do NOT delete the existing AIJob table.
Do NOT modify Prisma schema for this phase.

The existing database can contain old AIJob records; leave them untouched.

12. Error handling
Create centralized AI errors so the API consistently distinguishes:
- authentication failure
- validation failure
- AI provider failure
- invalid model output
- authorization failure
- action failure

Do not leak provider secrets or internal database details to the client.

13. Testing/security
Before integrating deeply into the UI, verify:
- authenticated business isolation
- cross-business project/task access is impossible
- malformed AI JSON is rejected
- invalid references are rejected
- model cannot execute arbitrary actions
- destructive actions require explicit confirmation
- missing GROQ_API_KEY produces a clean server error
- provider failures produce a clean API error

14. UI
Keep UI integration minimal during Phase 0.

Create reusable:
components/ai/PulseAiPanel.tsx
components/ai/AiActionConfirmation.tsx

Do not rebuild the entire dashboard.

The panel should be capable of displaying:
- assistant responses
- insights
- progress
- priorities
- generated plans
- proposed actions

Actions must display as proposals requiring confirmation.

15. Existing application
Do not unnecessarily rewrite existing workspace/project/task APIs.
Do not replace working authentication.
Do not duplicate existing business authorization logic unless creating a stricter AI-specific boundary.

16. Environment
Add only the necessary dependency/configuration.
GROQ_API_KEY must remain server-only.
Do not commit secrets.
Do not create NEXT_PUBLIC_GROQ_API_KEY.
